### 6. Problem tree from the visible materials alone
Root: transfer of unused visits (customer's own write).
- Hop A (transfer ← unfreeze). `giving_visits_to_family`: "Visits are not transferred until the giving package's freeze is lifted and it stands in active status." Record: package `status: 'frozen'`. Search "freeze is lifted / active status" → `lifting_a_freeze`: "A frozen package is unfrozen at the patient's request: it returns to active status". Mark: **state-derived** (the sentence names a state; note the wording "freeze is lifted" coincides with the unfreeze hub's own vocabulary — carried to the dependency-form scan).
- Hop B (transfer ← purchase for Marcus). Same doc: "Visits are not transferred until the recipient holds an active package of their own, bought and paid for." Records: Marcus has only expired/exhausted packages. Search "active package … bought … paid" → `same_tier_repurchase_sale`: "The patient holds an active package in their name with all of its visits available … the full price taken as a single payment". Mark: **state-derived**.
- Hop C (transfer ← past-due installment). `transferable_visit_balance`: "Before the transferable balance is worked out, every installment of the giving package whose due date has passed must stand paid in the package's history." Records: installments 1, 2 only; installment 3 due 2026-08-11. Search "installment … past due … paid" → `past_due_installment_collection`: "An installment … whose due date has passed and that has no installment payment in the package history is collected on the call". Mark: **state-derived**.
- Hop D (unfreeze ← past-due installment). `freeze_credit_days`: "The expiry extension on unfreezing is fixed only after the package's history carries an installment payment for every installment whose due date has passed". Same records, same depended-on doc. Mark: **state-derived**. Observation: the same paragraph continues "while one does not, the freeze days are limited to the days from the freeze start date to the due date of the first unpaid installment" — the visible text both gates the extension on payment and states a limited computation for the unpaid case; read with "only after", the order installment → unfreeze is the one consistent with the gate, and the medical-hold allowance ("the package's status … is frozen at the time of collection") is then also met.
Order: installment → unfreeze → transfer; purchase anywhere before transfer. No hop was pre-solved by a tool name, route or chain.

### Two-way counter-proof
- "Do only the transfer": excluded — the package is frozen (Hop A sentence), Marcus has no active package (Hop B sentence), installment 3 is unpaid (Hop C sentence); the user tool also needs `recipient_package_id`, which does not exist until the purchase.
- Unfreeze before collecting: excluded by "fixed only after" (Hop D); it would also remove the medical-hold allowance (package no longer frozen) and change the extension.
- Collect at the fall-back $752.00: excluded by the four installment factor docs, each findable from the records named above.
- Purchase at 10 % ($599.40) or at 37 % ($419.58): excluded by the stacking doc and the 35 % ceiling doc.
- Transfer all 16 (or the 8 shown before collection): excluded by the four reserve docs; the 8 currently shown in `visits_remaining` coincides numerically with the right answer only by accident (16 − 8 after the installment credit).
- Recipient object: the Core 8 expired package is a different tier; "same six-visit package" → Recovery 6.
